items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: It was Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon. I knew him up there.

ctx.x: Yes, he'd been up there at the absent house.

Yeah, ever since the absent house closed down and he's up there playing. Then his mother's up there too, you know. And I'm trying to think of some man, and I know so many guys, but I'm just like I was saying, like what's this guy's name? Moe. He's a clarinetist too, Moe. Noon, Noon, Noon, something like that. Not Noon, the business. The boy was playing the clarinetist and went to Chicago, Noon. It was Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon. I knew him up there. He was one of the boys around there too. And all there's…
That you would remember such as Joe Oliver.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: Right next door to me. That's over 20 years ago. Jimmy Noon was a player.

ctx.x: And he was right there, huh?
Right next door to me. That's over 20 years ago. Jimmy Noon was a player.
Oh, 50 years ago. Huh? It'd be 50 years ago, I bet, Jimmy Noon, huh?
